findings: Closed door frame and uninterrupted lower rail keep both dogs on the interior rug and both diners outside; table, chair feet and skyline establish a high apartment balcony. Rear viewpoint makes the plate-watching exclusion readable without duplicating the later action.

Neet has four separate grounded paws, fine leg shafts, full narrow connected torso, broad triangular ears and a compact rounded rump nub. No long tail or invented plume. Muzzle/glass contact is mostly hidden by this rear view, so no exact nose-pressure detail is claimed.

Buddy has continuous seated haunch-to-back-to-neck anatomy, grounded forepaws and folded hind support. His tail lies on the rug and tapers; head size is modest. The pale chest edge has a few short points, but no long hanging chest fringe, shag envelope or detached chest shape. Close dark torso and regional pale feet/muzzle remain distinct.

Perspective and warm finish are coherent, with no extra limbs or fused furniture. Sagar wears blue here and white in the later indoor pictures; this is a minor wardrobe continuity discrepancy, not a dog identity/anatomy or action defect.

findings: Neet has exactly two forepaws placed on top of the closed human fist and two fine hindlegs bearing weight on the rug. Shoulder, elbow, paw and upright trunk connections are continuous; his compact nub remains separate from the sofa.

Buddy has a full moderately elongated torso, substantial legs with clearance, four grounded feet and a connected raised neck. Nose meets the elbow region of the same continuous arm whose fist Neet braces. This reads as a moment between the repeated jumps, not an airborne pose.

The forearm continues behind Buddy’s head to its bent elbow and upper arm; the other human hand rests on the knee. No detached hands or shared dog limbs. Both separate mistaken strategies are immediately readable.

Smooth short torso washes replace the rough sheet’s body hatching. Buddy’s furnished muzzle and hanging ears preserve identity; the closer grooming treatment is somewhat simpler than the closing close-up but does not change the dog’s body or regional markings. Human crop is intentional, and all weight-bearing contacts remain visible.

findings: Buddy’s uninterrupted back, full ribcage and tucked pelvis rest on the rug. Two hind paws remain attributable to the folded hindquarter; one foreleg lies forward on the rug while the other bends upward from the far shoulder. No spare paw, detached shoulder or floating chest.

The lifted paw makes actual contact across the back of the loosely closed hand near the wrist/knuckle base. Curled human fingers and continuous wrist/forearm read clearly; the contact is gentle rather than a head-on knuckle collision, consistent with the closing paw-touch gesture. No naan is visible.

Torso surface has fine restrained short directional texture with a smooth silhouette, not curls, engraved long strands or enlarged fur volume. The furnished brow, ear edge and pale moustache/beard remain regional. Tail is a modest taper lying on the rug.

The low close view and warm lamplight shift from comic instruction to affectionate learned behavior. Human shoe, trouser leg, chair and forearm have coherent scale and support; the hand is attached to the visible arm. Neet is outside this crop, so this picture makes no claim about his resting pose.
